case.case_title: Channa Pieris and Others v. Attorney-General and Others (Ratawesi Peramuna Case)
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1994] 1 Sri LR.

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioners were brought before a judge of the nearest competent court according to procedure established by law as required by Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners claimed that their rights under Article 13(2) were violated because they were not properly produced before a judge and were held in custody without lawful judicial orders.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents contended that the petitioners were produced before the magistrate and that the detention orders were lawful.
key_facts: Petitioners were detained after arrest at various police stations.
Some petitioners were produced before the Fort Magistrate after several days.
There were allegations that production before the judge was only technical and did not allow meaningful communication.
Detention orders were issued but were flawed and some were ultra vires.
The petitioners were held in custody without proper judicial authorization for periods.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court interpreted Article 13(2) as requiring real and effective production before a judge, not merely a technical or physical presence. The purpose is to allow the detainee to make representations and for the judge to apply judicial mind to the detention. Production that denies communication or legal representation violates Article 13(2).
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court found that the petitioners were not brought before a judge in a manner that fulfilled the constitutional requirement. Some were produced only in a technical sense, such as being kept outside the judge’s residence without opportunity to communicate or be represented. Detention orders lacked lawful basis and the petitioners were held without proper judicial orders.
principles_established: Production before a judge must be real and effective.
Technical or superficial production does not satisfy Article 13(2).
The detainee must have opportunity to communicate and seek legal representation.
Detention without lawful judicial order violates Article 13(2).
Judicial oversight is a safeguard against arbitrary detention.
precedents_cited: Sasanasiritissa Thero and Others v. De Silva and Others
Schiesser Case - European Court of Human Rights
Skoogstrom Case - European Court of Human Rights
McGoff Case - European Court of Human Rights
Ekanayake v. Herath Banda and Others
Withanachchi v. Cyril Herath and Others

outcome.holding: The Court declared that the fundamental rights guaranteed by Article 13(2) were violated as the petitioners were not brought before a judge in accordance with procedure established by law.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) is central to the Court's reasoning on the legality of detention after arrest, ensuring judicial oversight and protection against unlawful detention.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioners were held in custody without proper judicial orders and were produced before judges only in a technical manner that denied them meaningful communication or legal representation.
